question.prompt:
In triangle \(ABC,\) point \(F\) divides side \(AC\) in the ratio \(1:2.\) Let \(E\) be the point where side \(BC\) meets \(AG,\) where \(G\) is the midpoint of \(BF.\) Then \(E\) divides \(BC\) in the ratio:

[Figure 1](figures/1971_AMC_12_Q26_question_fig1.svg)

solutions.explanation:
A midpoint suggests equal areas: triangles with equal bases on the same line and a common altitude have equal areas. Write \([XYZ]\) for the area of triangle \(XYZ\). The given division is \(AF:FC=1:2\), so \(AF/AC=1/3\).

Since \(G\) is the midpoint of \(BF\), the medians \(AG\) in triangle \(ABF\) and \(EG\) in triangle \(EBF\) give
\[
[ABG]=[AFG],\qquad [EBG]=[EFG].
\]
Point \(G\) lies on segment \(AE\), so adding these equalities combines the small triangles into
\[
[ABE]=[ABG]+[EBG]
=[AFG]+[EFG]=[AFE].
\]
Now triangles \(AFE\) and \(ACE\) have bases \(AF\) and \(AC\) on the same line and share the altitude from \(E\). Therefore
\[
\frac{[AFE]}{[ACE]}=\frac{AF}{AC}=\frac13.
\]
Triangles \(ABE\) and \(ACE\) share the altitude from \(A\) to \(BC\), so their area ratio is also their base ratio. Consequently,
\[
\frac{BE}{EC}
=\frac{[ABE]}{[ACE]}
=\frac13.
\]
All these areas and side lengths are positive in the given triangle. Thus \(\boxed{BE:EC=1:3}\), choice \(\mathrm{B}\).
solutions.title: Use the midpoint to compare areas

solutions.explanation:
Draw through \(F\) a line parallel to \(AE\), meeting \(CE\) at \(H\). Because \(F\) lies inside side \(CA\) of triangle \(CAE\), the parallel line meets the interior of side \(CE\). This construction lets us use both the given division of \(AC\) and the midpoint of \(BF\).

The ratio \(AF:FC=1:2\) gives \(CF/CA=2/3\). Applying the parallel-segment theorem in triangle \(CAE\), with \(FH\parallel AE\), gives
\[
\frac{CH}{CE}=\frac{CF}{CA}=\frac23.
\]
Thus
\[
EH=CE-CH=\frac13 CE.
\]
Next consider triangle \(BFH\). The points on its base occur in the order \(B,E,H\), and \(GE\parallel FH\) because \(G,E,A\) are collinear. Parallel lines divide the two sides proportionally, so
\[
\frac{BE}{EH}=\frac{BG}{GF}=1.
\]
Hence \(BE=EH=CE/3\), and therefore \(\boxed{BE:EC=1:3}\), choice \(\mathrm{B}\).
solutions.title: Create proportional segments with a parallel line
